cf.title: Eliminate redundant outer-join clone clauses after constant propagation

input.subject: Eliminate redundant outer-join clone clauses after constant propagation

verdict_reasoning: The proposal does not name a target branch, and the answer decides the design (standards-compat-1). ABI stability is the only reason given to avoid the v3 RestrictInfo field, and that limit applies only to back branches. Message #1 also shows no query or timing that got worse after f4002899 (demand-1). Both are fixable, but a committer would likely ask for them before reading the nullability check.

brief.title: Drop redundant outer-join clone clauses after constant propagation
brief.problem: Commit f4002899 fixed a wrong-result bug by keeping every constant-propagated outer-join clone clause, marked with norm_selec > 1. This leaves unnecessary join filters in join orders where the clause is redundant. An earlier fix (v3) avoided this by adding a RestrictInfo field, but that breaks ABI and cannot be back-patched.
brief.proposed_design: When the planner builds the restriction list for a join or parameterized path, it omits clone clauses marked norm_selec > 1 unless a deferred, pushed-down outer join may already have null-extended the clause's outer operand. The check uses existing RestrictInfo and SpecialJoinInfo fields only. The clause stays distributed and available during join-order search.
user_visible_surface: Plan changes: some queries with outer joins and constant-propagated equalities lose redundant join filters and may get different join orders.
author_claims: Restores removal of unnecessary join filters that f4002899 left in place.
Keeps the correctness fix from f4002899.
Adds no field to RestrictInfo, so the ABI does not change.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. No one has replied yet.
unclear: The material does not say whether the author intends this for back-patching or for master only.
No numbers show the planning-time cost of the extra check or the execution-time gain.
The material does not say how norm_selec > 1 is kept distinct from other uses of that value.
No new regression test targets the deferred pushed-down outer join case beyond changed plans in join.out.

prior_attempts.title: Redundant qualifier elimination
prior_attempts.quote: It would impose nontrivial costs on every query --- roughly O(N^2) in the number of restriction clauses --- in order to fix badly-written queries, and that is not a tradeoff I like.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane opposed the patch even with fixes, because it adds roughly O(N^2) planning cost in the number of restriction clauses to every query to handle badly written queries. Denis Smirnov showed that removing a duplicate volatile clause such as nextval('s') = 1 changes query results, and that the patch does not fix the JIT regression in the original report. The author accepted the feedback.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P4 compared every base restriction clause against all others with equal() for every query. This patch tests only clone clauses already marked norm_selec > 1 when it builds a join or parameterized-path restriction list.

objections.title: Plan-changing optimization framed around back-branch ABI limits
objections.failure_scenario: A user on a stable branch applies a minor release that contains this patch. A query with outer joins and a constant-propagated equality gets a different join order and runs slower. The user finds out from production latency after an upgrade that was expected to be safe.
objections.argument: Message #1 gives ABI stability as the only reason to avoid the v3 RestrictInfo field, and that constraint applies only to back-branches. The proposal does not say whether it targets master or stable branches. Postgres does not usually back-patch planner optimizations that change plans, and join.out shows the plans change. On master, a new field is allowed, so the ABI argument for this design does not hold there.
objections.author_must_show: Is this patch meant for back-branches, and if it is only for master, why not use the clearer v3 RestrictInfo field instead?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 gives ABI as the only reason to avoid the v3 field and does not name a target branch. The ABI limit applies only to back branches, so the question stands.

objections.title: No evidence the leftover join filters cost any user anything
objections.failure_scenario: A committer adds a second, subtle nullability check to clause selection in relnode.c, in the area where f4002899 just fixed a wrong-result bug. The only gain is dropping a redundant equality filter, because the derived INNERVAR = CONSTANT already applies. If the new check misses a commuting-join case, users get wrong results, and they find out from bug reports.
objections.argument: Message #1 gives no field report, no -general or -bugs thread and no query that got slower after f4002899. It also gives no execution or planning-time numbers. The only evidence is changed plans in join.out, which show the plan differs but not that it is faster. With f4002899, the leftover clause adds no selectivity, so the main remaining cost is one cheap filter per row.
objections.author_must_show: Which real queries got measurably slower after f4002899, and by how much does this patch improve their planning or execution time?

critic.reasoning: The patch restores an optimization that existed before f4002899, and the join.out changes include different join orders, so the gain may be more than one filter. But message #1 shows no query or timing, so the request for numbers stands.

other_surviving.title: Correctness depends on norm_selec > 1 used as a semantic flag
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A later patch sets norm_selec above 1 on some other clause for a selectivity reason, for example to stop double counting. The new relnode.c check treats that clause as a redundant clone and leaves it out of a join restriction list. The query returns extra rows, and nothing fails until a user reports a wrong result.
other_surviving.argument: norm_selec is a cached selectivity, and f4002899 set it above 1 only so the kept clause adds no selectivity. The patch now makes that value decide whether a qual is evaluated at all. Message #1 gives ABI as the reason to avoid a dedicated field, but that limit applies only to back branches. On master an explicit flag would fail loudly if misused, and the material does not say which branch this patch targets.
other_surviving.author_must_show: If this targets master, why is overloading norm_selec better than an explicit RestrictInfo flag, and what stops other code from setting norm_selec above 1?

critic.reasoning: The scenario is weaker than stated, because norm_selec > 1 already means "redundant clause" in the planner and predates f4002899. But that marker has only affected selectivity so far, and the patch makes it decide whether a qual is evaluated.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Second copy of outer-join nullability reasoning in relnode.c
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A future change to outer-join commutation adds a new deferral case or changes how commute_below_l or syn_righthand is filled. incompatible_relids is updated, but this separate check is not. A clone clause is dropped at a level where the outer operand was already null-extended, which gives wrong results with no error.
other_surviving.argument: Message #1 builds the check from six RestrictInfo and SpecialJoinInfo fields, and the check runs at restriction-list time. That restates rules that clone and incompatible_relids handling already encode elsewhere. The area just had a wrong-result bug (f4002899). The only tests are changed plans in join.out, and none targets the deferred pushed-down outer join case.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which regression tests exercise the deferred pushed-down outer join case, so that a later commutation change that breaks this check fails visibly?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 confirms the check is derived separately from six existing fields at restriction-list time. The proposal does not show what fails if commutation rules change and this check is not updated.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Back-patch shaped design for a plan-changing optimization
refuted.failure_scenario: If this goes to stable branches, users on a minor update see join orders change for outer-join queries with constant equalities, and some may regress. If it goes to master only, the project keeps a design that avoids a struct field for an ABI reason that does not apply there.
refuted.argument: Message #1 presents ABI safety as the main gain over v3, which suggests a back-patch target. Back branches usually take wrong-result fixes, and f4002899 already fixed the wrong result. The redundant join filter is a cost issue, and no numbers show planning or execution gains that would justify plan changes in a stable branch.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this meant for back branches, and if so, which measured slowdown from the f4002899 join filters justifies plan changes in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. Its request for numbers is covered by demand-1.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The design avoids a new RestrictInfo field for ABI reasons and gives norm_selec > 1 a second meaning.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: join.out shows dropped join filters and different join orders for outer-join queries.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #1 presents ABI safety as the gain over v3 but does not name a target branch.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: relnode.c gains a separate outer-join nullability check built from six RestrictInfo and SpecialJoinInfo fields.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The check runs when the planner builds join and parameterized-path restriction lists; no planning-time numbers are given.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is this patch meant for back branches or for master only?
If it targets master only, why is reusing norm_selec > 1 better than the explicit RestrictInfo field from v3?
Which queries got measurably slower after f4002899, and how much does this patch improve their planning or execution time?
Which regression test exercises the deferred pushed-down outer join case, so that a later commutation change that breaks the check fails visibly?
What stops other planner code from setting norm_selec above 1 on a clause that must still be evaluated?

committability.owner_note: Needs a committer who knows outer-join commutation, clone clauses and incompatible_relids handling in the planner. No one has replied to message #1.
committability.liability: Wrong results for outer-join queries if the check misses a deferral case, on every branch that receives the patch. Later commutation changes must keep this check in step.
committability.author_follow_up: The author wrote v3 for the original wrong-result bug and returned with this follow-up, which suggests continued involvement.

priority.reason: The patch is small and touches one planner file, but it sits where f4002899 just fixed a wrong-result bug. The target branch must be settled first, because it decides whether reusing norm_selec is justified.

provisional_note: Without the code, it could not be judged whether the nullability check covers every deferred pushed-down outer join case or what it costs at planning time. The two level 2 objections on norm_selec reuse and the duplicated nullability reasoning were not evaluated.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Disallow outer-level and WHERE-clause aggregates in GRAPH_TABLE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes parser gaps where an outer-level aggregate in a GRAPH_TABLE COLUMNS list or graph pattern WHERE clause led to "Aggref found in non-Agg plan node". Later versions added GRAPH_TABLE ParseExprKind values, rejected subqueries in GRAPH_TABLE early, and taught level-aware walkers to treat GraphPropertyRef like a Var.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the CF entry and cited commit b1f106c80cbe; the visible messages do not say what that commit did. Before that, Tom Lane said he expected PGQ to be reverted for 19 after concerns raised by Andres, so he had stopped reviewing the fix. He also objected to GraphPropertyRef, a node that acts like a Var but is not one, and proposed replacing it with Vars that point at a second RTE.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I will say that I do not like GraphPropertyRef one bit and that the best way forward if we're not building an emergency band-aid for 19 is to get rid of it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fast path for empty relids in check_outerjoin_delay()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an early return to check_outerjoin_delay() when the given relids are empty, the same exit already taken when there are no special joins. The author presented it as a readability change with no expected performance gain.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that more special cases and fast paths make the code harder to read and maintain. Tom Lane agreed the patch should be rejected: it is unlikely to help performance, does not improve readability, and empty relids reach the function only from check_equivalence_delay. Tom suggested a larger refactoring of check_outerjoin_delay and the SpecialJoinInfo structures, and closed the entry when no follow-on patch came by the end of the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Anyway, I concur with Peter that the patch you've presented should
probably be rejected: I doubt it's a win performance-wise and I don't
see that it adds anything to readability either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove redundant NULL check in clause_selectivity_ext()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Remove the NULL clause check in clause_selectivity_ext(), which carries a "can this still happen?" comment, because no core caller seems to pass a NULL clause. The author listed each core call site to support this.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the check kept because it is cheap and extensions call clauselist_selectivity and related functions and may rely on it not crashing on a NULL. He also said the list_length check proves nothing about NULL list elements, and that removing such checks one at a time without agreed invariants is not wise. David Rowley agreed, saying no speedup could be measured and no benchmark was given, and suggested marking the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Certainly, such an assumption could be argued to be a bug they
should fix; but I'm disinclined to make them jump through that
hoop for a vanishingly small performance improvement.

precedents_retrieved.title: Redundant qualifier elimination
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner drop a base-relation restriction clause when an equal() clause is already present, so a qual repeated in a JOIN's ON clause and the WHERE clause is not counted twice in selectivity. The check sits in add_base_clause_to_rel() and handles only identical quals.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane opposed the patch even with fixes, because it adds roughly O(N^2) planning cost in the number of restriction clauses to every query in order to handle badly written queries. Denis Smirnov showed that removing a duplicate volatile clause such as nextval('s') = 1 changes query results, and that the patch does not fix the JIT regression in the original report. The author accepted the feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It would impose nontrivial
costs on every query --- roughly O(N^2) in the number of restriction
clauses --- in order to fix badly-written queries, and that is not
a tradeoff I like.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PERF] Improve Cardinality Estimation for Joins with GROUP BY Having Single Clause
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes join selectivity estimation so that a subquery with a single-column GROUP BY is treated as unique on that column. The planner then takes the number of distinct values from the aggregate node's row estimate instead of the default of 200.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch because master already fixed the problem. Ilia Evdokimov showed that master at commit 122a9af gives the correct estimate without the patch, and the author pointed to commit e983ee9 as the fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I initially applied this patch on the master branch at commit f95da9f, but I have noticed that the latest master branch already includes a fix for this issue. A similar patch was recently committed in e983ee9 successfully resolving this issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove redundant initializations
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed removing code that sets each struct field to zero right after makeNode() or memset() has already zeroed the whole struct. He kept initializations that carry nontrivial comments or keep symmetry between branches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback after waiting on author for three weeks: the patch no longer applied on HEAD, and no rebased version was posted. Before that, Tom Lane objected that explicit initialization of every field is an intended style, which helps when adding a new field and avoids depending on all-zero-bits values. Noah Misch later supported the idea and offered to review it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This has been sitting in the CF app for three weeks waiting on author,
so I have marked this entry as RwF for now:

precedents_retrieved.title: Convert join OR clauses into UNION queries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The planner would rewrite a query whose WHERE clause has an OR with arms that each reference a different joined relation into a UNION with one arm per relation. It removes duplicate rows by sort/unique on the CTIDs of the base relations, and it builds this as an extra path that competes on cost with the normal plan.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane, the patch author, said he was still not convinced that the unique-ification step is correct, and he would not work on it further without a proof. Noah Misch's review, with assertion failures and a case where planning was 170 times slower and the chosen plan 4.5 times slower, got no reply for a month, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
FWIW, my problem with this patch is that I remain unconvinced of the basic
correctness of the transform (specifically the unique-ification approach).

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve join selectivity estimation using extended statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses per-table extended statistics, mainly functional dependencies, when it estimates join selectivity in clausesel.c. It also tries to combine join clauses with relation-level filters in calc_joinrel_size_estimate to estimate conditional probabilities.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra found the design at the wrong level of abstraction. Clausesel.c handled extended statistics directly, dependencies were applied clause by clause in a fixed order and only on the inner relation, and he proposed handling all join clauses for a pair of relations at once in extended_stats.c. The author agreed it could be done better but posted no new version. In July the patch no longer compiled, and it still did not one commitfest later, so it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch includes some *very* interesting ideas, but I think it's does them too late and at the wrong level of abstraction.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent is the same idea. Message #1 reports one earlier attempt, v3 for the original wrong-result bug, which was set aside because a new RestrictInfo field breaks ABI. This patch adds no field, so that reason no longer applies. The P4 concern about planning cost could matter if the new check runs for every join restriction list, but the material gives no sign of quadratic cost, so I raise no objection from prior attempts.
Apart from the release-target question, the user-facing contract does not change: no syntax, no GUC, no catalog or pg_dump impact, and results stay the same by design.

The patch changes only planner logic in relnode.c and plan output in join.out. It adds no catalog, WAL, on-disk, wire-protocol or struct change, and it keeps RestrictInfo unchanged, so nothing persists or crosses a process boundary. Back-branch plan stability, if back-patching is intended, belongs to another angle.

The patch only changes which clone clauses the planner keeps in a join or parameterized path restriction list. It adds no privilege, role, view, log output or user-controlled input path, so this angle has no objection. A wrong plan here would give wrong results, which is a correctness concern and outside the security angle.
No committer has replied yet, so who would own this optimizer code is open. [P4] covers a different duplicate-qual check, and its O(N^2) cost reason does not apply here.

No existing feature, setting or extension removes redundant clone clauses in planner internals, so this angle has nothing to raise. The patch refines the norm_selec > 1 marker from f4002899 instead of adding a second mechanism. [P4] covers a different case: duplicate base quals and their O(N^2) cost.
Demand is the only open point from this angle. The plan changes alone do not show that users gain anything.
